findings.doc_quote: ChangeType is a union of literal value, C.* condition instance, glob string, or callable (value) -> bool .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/types/types.py:330 — "FalseySentinel | V | Condition[V | FalseySentinel] | ComparisonCondition[V | FalseySentinel] | None"; src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:763-765 — non-callable conditions compare by equality: `coerce_to_literal_type(actual, condition) == condition`
findings.explanation: ChangeType has no glob-string member. A string is an ordinary literal and compares exactly. The only automatic glob wrapping for this type is in ServiceDataWhere (predicates.py:700). The union also includes sentinels, None, and two-argument comparison conditions, which the page omits. Probe result: compare_value("light.kitchen", "light.*") returned False.
findings.suggested_fix: ChangeType is a union of a literal value (including None), a sentinel such as ANY_VALUE, a C.* condition instance, or a callable. A string literal compares exactly; use C.Glob for pattern matching. Only P.ServiceDataWhere auto-wraps glob strings.

findings.explanation: The dataclass field is named fn, not predicate. Probe result: P.Guard(predicate=...) raised TypeError: Guard.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'predicate'. Positional use works.

findings.doc_quote: condition accepts a literal value, a C.* condition instance, a glob string, or any callable (value) -> bool .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:321-322 — `extracted = self.source(value); return compare_value(extracted, self.condition)`; predicates.py:763-765 — equality comparison for non-callables, with no is_glob check
findings.explanation: P.ValueIs does not detect globs, so a string such as "light.*" compares literally and will not match "light.kitchen". The same applies to P.StateFrom, P.StateTo, P.AttrFrom and P.AttrTo, and to changed_from=/changed_to=, because bus.py:1757-1762 passes those values straight to these predicates. The page's own line 66 snippet comment says string literals compare exactly.
findings.suggested_fix: condition accepts a literal value, a C.* condition instance, or any callable (value) -> bool. A bare string compares exactly; for glob matching, pass C.Glob("light.*").

findings.doc_quote: When old_state is None , returns False even if the attribute is present on the new state.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:530-531 — `if value.payload.data.old_state is None: return get_attr_new(self.attr_name)(value) is not MISSING_VALUE`
findings.explanation: The code does the opposite. When old_state is None, it returns True if the attribute is present on new_state, and False only if the attribute is absent.
findings.suggested_fix: When old_state is None , returns True if the attribute is present on the new state, and False otherwise.

findings.doc_quote: Returns True when the string value contains substring , ignoring case.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/conditions.py:227 — `return isinstance(value, str) and self.substring in value`
findings.explanation: The check is case-sensitive. Probe result: C.Contains("Kit")("kitchen") returned False and C.Contains("kit")("kitchen") returned True.
findings.suggested_fix: Returns True when the string value contains substring (case-sensitive).

findings.doc_quote: collection must be a sequence, not a string. Passing a string raises TypeError .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/conditions.py:120-122 — `if isinstance(collection, str): raise ValueError("collection must be a sequence of values, not a string")`
findings.explanation: The validator raises ValueError, so code catching TypeError would miss it. Probe result: C.IsIn("abc") raised ValueError.
findings.suggested_fix: collection must be a sequence, not a string. Passing a string raises ValueError .

findings.doc_quote: Returns True when float(old) < threshold <= float(new) .
findings.explanation: The inequality boundaries are reversed. An old value equal to the threshold counts, and a new value equal to the threshold does not. Probe result: CrossedAbove(25)(25, 26) returned True and CrossedAbove(25)(24, 25) returned False; the page's formula gives the opposite for both.
findings.suggested_fix: Returns True when float(old) <= threshold < float(new) .

findings.doc_quote: The context dict from the event payload.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/events/base.py:31-32 — `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) class HassContext`; src/hassette/events/hass/hass.py:221 — `"context": HassContext(**event["context"])`
findings.explanation: HassContext is a frozen dataclass, so fields are read as attributes (context.id), not by dict key. The Returns column gives the correct type.
findings.suggested_fix: The HassContext object from the event payload.

findings.doc_quote: Excludes last_reported , last_updated , and last_changed by default.
findings.explanation: The default exclusion list has a fourth entry, context, which the page omits.
findings.suggested_fix: Excludes last_reported , last_updated , last_changed , and context by default.

summary: Most of the page is accurate: the signatures, accessor tables, literal coercion rules and operator shorthand all match the code, and the coercion and condition behavior was also confirmed with a runtime probe. Nine claims fail, seven of them high severity, clustered in glob-string handling (lines 9 and 28) and single-detail errors in the tables: the Guard field name, AttrDidChange with no old state, Contains case sensitivity, the IsIn/NotIn exception type, and the CrossedAbove boundaries. The two low-severity findings are the HassContext description and the incomplete get_all_changes default exclusion list.
